correctness.rationale: For every finite simple undirected base graph, arbitrary partition of base edges E=A disjoint B (empty allowed), and prime p, the graph-state cut matrix equals unsigned-incidence product C=U_A^T U_B exactly because two distinct base edges share at most one endpoint. Removing local internal phases, additive-character orthogonality makes reduced density rho_A equal p^{-|A|} on pairs differing by ker(C^T), yielding p^r equal nonzero eigenvalues p^{-r} (r=rank_Fp C). Left kernel U_A^T has one all-one vector for each component in characteristic 2, while in odd characteristic exactly bipartite components contribute alternating indicator vectors; isolated vertices are included. Rank pairing gives r=n-q_A-q_B+rank(T_A^T T_B) even for empty matrices and odd cycles. For K_n, n>=5, Hamilton A and odd-cycle connected complementary B give q_A=1, q_B=0 odd p, and q_A=q_B=1 with overlap [n mod2] at p2, yielding stated parity split and maximal odd-prime subsystem. Independently checked 2,280 n<=4 colored graph partitions and 27 Hamilton examples, distinct from unrestricted proof.
